paper_title: 2-Tier SimCSE Elevating BERT for Robust Sentence Embeddings
caption: : Figure 2: Accuracy comparison of different models on paraphrase sentiment, and STS tasks.
model_annotation: This vertical grouped bar chart illustrates an accuracy comparison of different models on paraphrase, sentiment, and STS tasks. The horizontal axis contains the categorical variables, representing five models ordered from left to right: Single-task_baseline, Baseline_with_Adaptive_Dropout, Unsupervised_SimCSE, Supervised_SimCSE, and 2-Tier SimCSE. The vertical value axis is labeled "Accuracy / Correlation" and uses a linear scale ranging from 0 to slightly above 0.8, with major tick labels at intervals of 0.2 and unmarked minor ticks every 0.05. For each model on the horizontal axis, the chart displays a grouped set of three adjacent vertical bars. According to the legend positioned at the top center, these bars represent three metrics, arranged left to right within each group: "Sentiment Acc." colored pale yellow, "STS Corr." colored pink, and "Paraphrase Acc." colored light blue. Looking at approximate values, the pale yellow "Sentiment Acc." bars range from roughly 0.48 for the Supervised_SimCSE model—which is the shortest bar in the chart—to about 0.53 for the Single-task_baseline. The pink "STS Corr." bars show a wider range, starting at approximately 0.50 for the Single-task_baseline and reaching about 0.81 for the 2-Tier SimCSE model, representing the tallest bar in the entire chart. The light blue "Paraphrase Acc." bars are visually consistent across all groups, ranging tightly between approximately 0.77 for Unsupervised_SimCSE and 0.79 for the Single-task_baseline. The model categories on the horizontal axis are not sorted in a strictly alphabetical or consistently ascending or descending numerical order across all metrics, and no individual bars are visually emphasized with distinct outlines or annotations, though a light gray background grid is present to assist with reading the values.
